rewrites.summary:
Connecticut is listed in a July 2026 national legal-risk map among the federation's Most Protective states — those that have “gone above and beyond” in safeguarding transgender people's rights — and equality-map research (data as of September 2026) counts Connecticut among the states whose healthcare “shield” laws protect trans people, their families and providers, including people travelling from states where care is banned, against out-of-state civil or criminal action.

Federal 2025 document and passport restrictions still apply to visitors here as in every state.
rewrites.tangentialFactors:
The July 2026 national legal-risk ranking is built from a rubric over thousands of tracked anti-trans bills (youth-care bans, bathroom bans, birth-certificate/driver-license restrictions, end of legal recognition); contrast tier: worst-law states carry up to 5-year prison terms (Idaho) or an arrest policy for gender-identity bathroom use (Florida).

National picture on the page: 16 states plus D.C. (38% of the trans population aged 13+) hold shield laws; 32 states plus 5 territories (56%) hold none; youth-care bans are tracked, some permanently blocked.
rewrites.localsOnly: The current sources record no Connecticut-specific resident details beyond the shield/refuge protection described in the summary.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes:
Unresolved: how the federal 2025 document and passport restrictions are handled in practice at Connecticut borders and how border officials treat corrected documents.

Unverified: whether the shield protections have in practice shielded a travelling visitor against out-of-state civil or criminal action, and how the “Most Protective” tier rubric weighs individual protections.
